reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.partition -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: none directly; the partition times 0 <= t_0 <= t_1 <= ... <= t_N of a simple
predictable process (textbook elementary integrand used to build the Ito integral of sec. 3/4).
Faithful Lean: a finite family of times indexed consistently with N (Fin (N+1) -> R or R_{>=0}),
monotone (nondecreasing suffices; strictly increasing is a harmless restriction since a zero-
length interval contributes nothing), nonnegative (or t_0 >= 0). Whether the times are bounded by
T is immaterial for the integral on [0,t] for t <= T (the integral up to t truncates). Not
harmless: no monotonicity (intervals ill-defined) or negative times (then measurability w.r.t.
F_{t_i} at negative times is meaningless unless the filtration is extended).

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.partition (ItoSimpleIntegrand.lean:34-35)

Reading: finite family of times indexed consistently with N, monotone, nonnegative; strict
increase harmless; bound by T immaterial. Lean: partition : Fin (N+1) -> R, with structure
constraints partition 0 = 0, StrictMono partition, partition (Fin.last N) <= T. All items
present. Representation choices: t_0 = 0 (instead of t_0 >= 0) and strict increase (instead of
nondecreasing) are normalisations of the same class of step functions (prepend a zero piece /
drop zero-length pieces); t_N <= T ties the step process to the horizon parameter T, harmless
because masterApprox uses growing horizons n+1 and integrals are taken up to t <= n+1.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Choices: (1) partition 0 = 0 rather than t_0 >= 0: any simple process with t_0 > 0 is the same
function with a zero-coefficient first piece on (0,t_0], so nothing is lost. (2) StrictMono rather
than monotone: a zero-length piece (t_i,t_i] is empty and contributes nothing to eval or to the
simple integral, so dropping it changes neither. (3) partition (last N) <= T: the step process is
tied to the horizon parameter T; consumers (masterApprox) use horizons n+1 -> oo and evaluate
integrals only at t <= n+1, so no integrand or time is excluded.

author_review.disagreements:
No disagreement on substance. The reviewer records "faithful"; I record "faithful with
representation choices" only to list explicitly the normalisations partition 0 = 0 (rather than
t_0 >= 0), strict monotonicity (rather than nondecreasing) and partition (last) <= T, each a
harmless normalisation of the same class of step functions. The difference is one of labelling.
